description: One-way ratchet on startup migrations that fail against a freshly provisioned database, read by scripts/verify-startup-migrations.mjs from the migrations block of /api/health/db. CI gates the whole backend suite on the startup step, and that step used to succeed whether or not any migration in it had failed, so a broken migration ran the suite against a partly applied schema. knownFailures freezes the set observed on a fresh CI database; totals.failureCeiling is the count and may only fall. Any failure not listed here fails the build. Lower the ceiling in the same change that fixes a migration - leaving headroom lets it refill silently.

classes.seed-foreign-key: Nine of the eleven: six INSERTs into agent_declarant_mappings and three into ledger_accounts pin company_id values that do not exist until companies are created. They fail on an empty database and succeed once the target company exists, which is why this gate is a frozen baseline rather than a demand for zero.
classes.schema-order: Two of the eleven are real: supplier_containers does not exist when a foreign key is added to it, and bales.erp_location_id does not exist when a foreign key is added to it. Both are ordering problems in the migration list and are the entries worth fixing first.

observedOn: Fresh database provisioned with drizzle-kit push, matching the CI sequence in .github/workflows/ci.yml (db:push, then node dist/index.js). The three factory_container_receipts ADD CONSTRAINT statements that used to fail only on a second startup were given the DO/duplicate_object guard in the same change, so a re-run against an already-migrated database now produces this same set of 11 rather than 14.
